description:
Atin (2026-10-06): a non-1.0 feature. Make the markdown viewer significantly better. Scope not yet pinned down; this ticket holds the intent until it is.

Current state (as of main d63b937f65):
- Native SwiftUI rendering via MarkdownUI (Sources/Panels/MarkdownPanelView.swift, MarkdownPanel.swift).
- Fenced blocks such as mermaid go through FencedCodeRenderer, which shells out to external CLI tools and inlines the result as an image. A missing tool shows a hint instead of the diagram.
- Live reload on file change, font scale, drop-to-open, a file-path header.
- Text selection is per segment; you cannot select across blocks.
- No find-in-document, no outline/TOC, no syntax-highlighted code, no verified anchor or relative-link navigation.
- The dark theme is weak (C11-127 covers making the theme configurable).

Candidate directions:
1. Reading quality: typography, spacing, a strong dark theme, syntax-highlighted code, wide tables.
2. Navigation: outline sidebar, find (Cmd+F), heading anchors, relative links that open in a c11 markdown tab, scroll position kept across reloads.
3. Fidelity: full GFM (task lists, footnotes, callouts), frontmatter, math, local images, Mermaid without an external tool.
4. Agent-native: CLI to scroll to a heading, read the visible section, highlight a passage, report what the operator is looking at.

Decided (Atin, 2026-10-06):
- Renderer: move to a WKWebView renderer (markdown-it or similar with bundled Mermaid, KaTeX and highlight.js; cross-block selection and find come free). Replaces MarkdownUI.
- Scope: directions 1-4 above, plus a read-only source-view toggle.
- Editing is handled by an "open in external markdown app" button in the markdown toolbar, styled like the browser's open-in-default-browser button (arrow.up.right.square, BrowserPanelView.openInExternalBrowserButton); it opens the file with the default .md app. No in-app editor (C11-344 cancelled).
- Theming (round 2 feedback): light and dark at minimum, built as a theme registry so further themes drop in later. Absorbs C11-127.
- Font size: first-class, with Cmd+ / Cmd- / Cmd0, a visible control with a fixed-width readout, reading position kept across reflow, persisted like today's markdown.fontScale.lastUsed.
- Zoom keys stay the app-wide ones: Cmd= / Cmd- / Cmd0 already route through AppDelegate's zoom shortcut handler to TabManager.zoomInFocusedMarkdown / zoomOutFocusedMarkdown / resetZoomFocusedMarkdown. The WKWebView rewrite keeps that path and drives the markdown font scale; WKWebView's own page zoom must not intercept the keys.
- Typeface (round 3): font families are theme tokens, so a theme can carry its own type, plus an operator typeface choice (reading serif / sans / mono) that overrides the theme's default, per tab, last-used as the default.
- No diff or change-tracking UI. Live reload keeps the reader's scroll position silently.
- Prototype first: clickable HTML mockups on a real repo plan file, iterated with Atin before any plan.

Related: C11-127 (markdown light/dark theme) folds into or sits under this ticket.

Next step: prototype discovery (tone-prototype), then plan.
title: Markdown viewer: a significantly better reading surface (post-1.0)
